html:
SMTO-AUT-0021 — The saved Google account entry is damaged or the wrong kind

GUID: 86c6bed7-6267-5ebf-b32c-a7e403a0d242
Slug: google-account-invalid
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • The entry SMTO was told to use isn't a valid connected Google account. It may be a different kind of entry, or its saved details were changed by hand or are incomplete. SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store, check that the name you gave SMTO belongs to an entry described as “Google Workspace authorization for” an email address. Only those entries are connected Google accounts; SMTO stops if the name points to an app setup or another kind of entry.
  2. Ask SMTO to reconnect that same Google account under the same name, and sign in on Google's page with the same email address. Reconnecting has Google confirm who you are, so SMTO can rebuild the entry from details it can trust.
  3. Don't try to fix the entry by editing its value or display name in Parameter Store. SMTO only trusts account details that come from Google's sign-in, so hand edits can't make the entry valid.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page says your email is connected, and your request runs without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the Google account entry yourself; Gmail, Calendar and Drive may all rely on it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Google account record is not a google_account (or supported legacy Gmail) profile, or it fails account-profile validation (fields, identity, feature and scope consistency, token state or expiry format).

What this means

  • The selected account record has the wrong profile type or fails the stored-account schema and identity/token requirements. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The selected account record has the wrong profile type or fails the stored-account schema and identity/token requirements.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the saved profile type and public authorization status; use provider verification for identity or token repair.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the record in Parameter Store: profile_type must be google_account with a valid email and subject, authorized_features exactly derived from granted_scopes, tokens present when authorization_state is available, a timezone-aware expires_at, and no extra fields. Don't hand-repair identity fields; reconnect the same account_key through auth.google_connect so a provider-verified identity and token bundle are saved, and if the record is too damaged for that, remove it and connect again.
  • Reconnect through auth.google_connect to save a provider-verified identity and token bundle.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account is saved through verified authorization and passes account-profile validation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
